newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Malbak unbundling on track via Stalcor sale.
newsitem.headline: Malbak unbundling on track via Stalcor sale.

text.p: The unbundling of Malbak Ltd gathered pace on Tuesday with the announcement that Baldwins Steel had bought a controlling stake in its unlisted Stalcor subsidiary for 43 million rand.
Johan van Niekerk, marketing director of Baldwins, a division of Dorbyl, said his company had purchased an initial 70 percent interest and had an option to increase this at a later date.
"We do have an option...It is part of our planning (to increase our stake," van Niekerk told Reuters.
The disposals by Malbak of its unlisted subsidiaries form part of the group's decision to unbundle its assets in a bid to unlock the value of its underlying investments.
In terms of listed investments Malbak has decided to distribute the shares it owns in these to shareholders.
Malbak said last week it would make an announcement soon on plans to sell its unlisted units following reports it might sell Defy to Electrolux of Sweden.
Swedish business daily Dagens Industri said Electrolux had placed a bid for Defy believed to be worth between 320 and 480 million crowns (200 to 300 million rand).

But acting chief executive Peter Beningfield declined to be drawn on the report saying the group was likely to put out a statement this week. He said, however, that Malbak remained on schedule to make a distribution to shareholders by the end of March or early April.

Malbak has said in the past that the sale of three of its unlisted units, Stalcor, Eagle Freight and Tedelex would generate more than 120 million rand. The sale of all unlisted investments, which also includes Malbak Motor Holdings, ICL (SA), Amalgamated Appliances, is expected to exceed 700 million rand.
In January it said Eagle Freight had secured German firm Thyssen Haniel Logistic GMbH as a 35 percent stakeholder.

Current Eagle Freight management bought the firm for an undisclosed sum which the company says was over 50 million rand, but has now sold 35 percent of the group to Thyssen Haniel Logistic, which is the transport and logistics arm of conglomerate Thyssen AG.
Listed companies in which Malbak has a major stake include Foodcorp, Kohler, South African Druggists, Ellerine and New Clicks.

Dorbyl said on Tuesday the purchase of Stalcor, an official distributor for Columbus Stainless and Hullet Aluminium, was in line with its strategy to penetrate the high growth stainless steel and aluminium markets.
It said the partnership would complement Baldwins Steel's core business of stocking and processing carbon steel products, it said.
